answer: Glacier delay registration: each new agent identity must solve a unique challenge derived from the current chain head, then remain inactive for a randomized holding period before gaining write access. A wharf-side routing table binds that identity to one immutable outbound address, so re-registering after rotation requires re-solving from scratch. The jetty admission queue admits identities slowly in proportion to recent creation rate. Attacker cost: continuous challenge solving plus stalled throughput per identity, scaling linearly with each sybil.
